## Q00825 — Peer-to-Peer vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

A team designing the Flight Booking System is split between **Peer-to-Peer** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Users of the Flight Booking System should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Peer-to-Peer** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical. Peer-to-Peer centers on Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode and peer request/reply and discovery/search; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.

In the Smart Traffic Platform, Peer-to-Peer is used as described: Users of the Traffic Management Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Availability** because distributes both demand and service/resource provision across peers; overlapping peer capabilities provide alternatives when one peer disappears.
Threatened: **Security** because decentralization makes trust, consistency, backup, recovery and security management harder; small networks may not achieve expected qualities.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q00849 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

An architect claims that once Peer-to-Peer is selected for the Smart Traffic Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **attachments can change at runtime** and the weakness **decentralization makes trust, consistency, backup, recovery and security management harder; small networks may not achieve expected qualities**. Construct an edge case where the intended mechanism is missing, overloaded or becomes a single dependency and show why the desired end-to-end quality is not achieved.

## Q00850 — Peer-to-Peer vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

A team designing the Smart Traffic Platform is split between **Peer-to-Peer** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Users of the Traffic Management Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Peer-to-Peer** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical. Peer-to-Peer centers on Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode and peer request/reply and discovery/search; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q00875 — Peer-to-Peer vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Social Network  

A team designing the Social Network is split between **Peer-to-Peer** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Users of the Social Network should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Peer-to-Peer** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical. Peer-to-Peer centers on Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode and peer request/reply and discovery/search; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q00876 — Peer-to-Peer (Hard, 6 marks)

Smart Home Platform: Users of the Smart Home Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

- Architectural problem: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical.
- Mechanism: distributes both demand and service/resource provision across peers; overlapping peer capabilities provide alternatives when one peer disappears.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode) and relation/connector (peer request/reply and discovery/search) to the concrete Smart Home Platform.
- Likely enhanced quality: Availability. Likely trade-off: Security.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

## Q00878 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Smart Home Platform  

In the Smart Home Platform, Peer-to-Peer is used as described: Users of the Smart Home Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Availability** because distributes both demand and service/resource provision across peers; overlapping peer capabilities provide alternatives when one peer disappears.
Threatened: **Security** because decentralization makes trust, consistency, backup, recovery and security management harder; small networks may not achieve expected qualities.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q00905 — Peer-to-Peer vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

A team designing the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform is split between **Peer-to-Peer** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Users of the Security Monitoring Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Peer-to-Peer** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical. Peer-to-Peer centers on Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode and peer request/reply and discovery/search; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

In the Medical Imaging Platform, Peer-to-Peer is used as described: Users of the Imaging Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Availability** because distributes both demand and service/resource provision across peers; overlapping peer capabilities provide alternatives when one peer disappears.
Threatened: **Security** because decentralization makes trust, consistency, backup, recovery and security management harder; small networks may not achieve expected qualities.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q00929 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **attachments can change at runtime** and the weakness **decentralization makes trust, consistency, backup, recovery and security management harder; small networks may not achieve expected qualities**. ## Q00930 — Peer-to-Peer vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

A team designing the Medical Imaging Platform is split between **Peer-to-Peer** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Users of the Imaging Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Peer-to-Peer** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical. Peer-to-Peer centers on Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode and peer request/reply and discovery/search; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Auction Platform  

A team designing the Online Auction Platform is split between **Peer-to-Peer** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Users of the Auction Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Peer-to-Peer** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical. Peer-to-Peer centers on Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode and peer request/reply and discovery/search; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q00956 — Peer-to-Peer (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

Supply Chain Platform: Users of the Supply Chain Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Peer-to-Peer** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: let equal distributed entities organize and share resources/services without making a single peer critical.
- Mechanism: distributes both demand and service/resource provision across peers; overlapping peer capabilities provide alternatives when one peer disappears.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Peer, optional specialized peer/supernode) and relation/connector (peer request/reply and discovery/search) to the concrete Supply Chain Platform.
- Likely enhanced quality: Availability. Likely trade-off: Security.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q00957 — Peer-to-Peer (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

For the Supply Chain Platform, assume the architect has chosen Peer-to-Peer to address this requirement: Users of the Supply Chain Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: each participating user device or node that contributes and requests the shared resource is a Peer; a discovery node or supernode is optional, not the owner of all resources. A Peer discovers another participant and directly requests/provides the resource through peer request/reply connections, while attachments may change as peers join or leave.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q00958 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

In the Supply Chain Platform, Peer-to-Peer is used as described: Users of the Supply Chain Platform should be able to contribute and directly share a resource with one another. Participants may join or leave dynamically, and no single participant should be essential to the service.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Availability** because distributes both demand and service/resource provision across peers; overlapping peer capabilities provide alternatives when one peer disappears.
Threatened: **Security** because decentralization makes trust, consistency, backup, recovery and security management harder; small networks may not achieve expected qualities.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q00959 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

</details>

## Q00961 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must integrate with online banking provider and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Service-Oriented Architecture** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network.
- Mechanism: consumers use published service contracts; registries hide provider identity/location, ESBs route/transform messages, and orchestration coordinates workflows.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB, optional service registry, optional orchestration server) and relation/connector (SOAP, REST request/reply, asynchronous messaging) to the concrete Student Portal.
- Likely enhanced quality: Interoperability. Likely trade-off: Performance.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q00962 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Service-Oriented Architecture to address this requirement: The Student Portal must integrate with online banking provider and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the scenario application is the Service Consumer, while each independently managed external capability is a Service Provider exposing a published network interface or contract. The consumer invokes that contract using REST/SOAP or messaging; an ESB, registry, or orchestration service is included only if the scenario needs routing, discovery, transformation, or workflow coordination.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q00985 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Flight Booking System  

A team designing the Flight Booking System is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Flight Booking System must integrate with airline/payment service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Service-Oriented Architecture** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network. Service-Oriented Architecture centers on Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB and SOAP; **Broker** instead addresses: let distributed service users invoke providers without knowing provider identity or location. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: clients should not know which distributed server provides the requested service.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

## Q01008 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

In the Smart Traffic Platform, Service-Oriented Architecture is used as described: The Traffic Management Platform must integrate with mapping/weather service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Interoperability** because consumers use published service contracts; registries hide provider identity/location, ESBs route/transform messages, and orchestration coordinates workflows.
Threatened: **Performance** because middleware adds overhead and failure points; independent providers can evolve outside your control and services may give no performance guarantees.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01009 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

An architect claims that once Service-Oriented Architecture is selected for the Smart Traffic Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Traffic Management Platform must integrate with mapping/weather service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **services expose published interfaces** and the weakness **middleware adds overhead and failure points; independent providers can evolve outside your control and services may give no performance guarantees**. Construct an edge case where the intended mechanism is missing, overloaded or becomes a single dependency and show why the desired end-to-end quality is not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01010 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

A team designing the Smart Traffic Platform is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Traffic Management Platform must integrate with mapping/weather service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Service-Oriented Architecture** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network. Service-Oriented Architecture centers on Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB and SOAP; **Broker** instead addresses: let distributed service users invoke providers without knowing provider identity or location. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: clients should not know which distributed server provides the requested service.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

## Q01012 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Ride-Hailing Platform

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the scenario application is the Service Consumer, while each independently managed external capability is a Service Provider exposing a published network interface or contract. ## Q01061 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform: The Security Monitoring Platform must integrate with threat-intelligence service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Service-Oriented Architecture** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network.
- Mechanism: consumers use published service contracts; registries hide provider identity/location, ESBs route/transform messages, and orchestration coordinates workflows.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB, optional service registry, optional orchestration server) and relation/connector (SOAP, REST request/reply, asynchronous messaging) to the concrete Security Monitoring Platform.
- Likely enhanced quality: Interoperability. Likely trade-off: Performance.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

## Q01063 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

In the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform, Service-Oriented Architecture is used as described: The Security Monitoring Platform must integrate with threat-intelligence service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Interoperability** because consumers use published service contracts; registries hide provider identity/location, ESBs route/transform messages, and orchestration coordinates workflows.
Threatened: **Performance** because middleware adds overhead and failure points; independent providers can evolve outside your control and services may give no performance guarantees.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01064 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

An architect claims that once Service-Oriented Architecture is selected for the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Security Monitoring Platform must integrate with threat-intelligence service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **services expose published interfaces** and the weakness **middleware adds overhead and failure points; independent providers can evolve outside your control and services may give no performance guarantees**. Construct an edge case where the intended mechanism is missing, overloaded or becomes a single dependency and show why the desired end-to-end quality is not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01065 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform  

A team designing the Cybersecurity Monitoring Platform is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Security Monitoring Platform must integrate with threat-intelligence service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Service-Oriented Architecture** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network. Service-Oriented Architecture centers on Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB and SOAP; **Broker** instead addresses: let distributed service users invoke providers without knowing provider identity or location. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: clients should not know which distributed server provides the requested service.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

## Q01088 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

In the Medical Imaging Platform, Service-Oriented Architecture is used as described: The Imaging Platform must integrate with hospital/PACS service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Interoperability** because consumers use published service contracts; registries hide provider identity/location, ESBs route/transform messages, and orchestration coordinates workflows.
Threatened: **Performance** because middleware adds overhead and failure points; independent providers can evolve outside your control and services may give no performance guarantees.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.

</details>

## Q01089 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

An architect claims that once Service-Oriented Architecture is selected for the Medical Imaging Platform, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Imaging Platform must integrate with hospital/PACS service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **services expose published interfaces** and the weakness **middleware adds overhead and failure points; independent providers can evolve outside your control and services may give no performance guarantees**. Construct an edge case where the intended mechanism is missing, overloaded or becomes a single dependency and show why the desired end-to-end quality is not achieved.

</details>

## Q01090 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Medical Imaging Platform  

A team designing the Medical Imaging Platform is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Imaging Platform must integrate with hospital/PACS service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Service-Oriented Architecture** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network. Service-Oriented Architecture centers on Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB and SOAP; **Broker** instead addresses: let distributed service users invoke providers without knowing provider identity or location. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: clients should not know which distributed server provides the requested service.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

## Q01115 — Service-Oriented Architecture vs Broker (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Online Auction Platform  

A team designing the Online Auction Platform is split between **Service-Oriented Architecture** and **Broker** for the following requirement:
The Auction Platform must integrate with payment/shipping service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Service-Oriented Architecture** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network. Service-Oriented Architecture centers on Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB and SOAP; **Broker** instead addresses: let distributed service users invoke providers without knowing provider identity or location. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: clients should not know which distributed server provides the requested service.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_4_CCPatterns_Broker.pdf

</details>

## Q01116 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Supply Chain Platform  

Supply Chain Platform: The Supply Chain Platform must integrate with supplier/logistics service and other independently managed services using published network interfaces, even though the providers may use different technologies and evolve independently.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Service-Oriented Architecture** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: integrate independently provided, heterogeneous or external services through published interfaces over a network.
- Mechanism: consumers use published service contracts; registries hide provider identity/location, ESBs route/transform messages, and orchestration coordinates workflows.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Service provider, Service consumer, optional ESB, optional service registry, optional orchestration server) and relation/connector (SOAP, REST request/reply, asynchronous messaging) to the concrete Supply Chain Platform.
- Likely enhanced quality: Interoperability. Likely trade-off: Performance.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q01121 — Publish-Subscribe (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must notify an unknown and changing set of interested users/components whenever a seat becomes available in a preferred class, without the event producer knowing every recipient.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Publish-Subscribe** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: distribute events from producers to an unknown or changing set of interested recipients without producers knowing recipient identities.
- Mechanism: decouples producers from consumers so subscribers can be added/removed without changing publisher correctness.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Publisher component, Subscriber component, event distributor / publish-subscribe connector) and relation/connector (publish-subscribe connector with announce/listen roles) to the concrete Student Portal.
- Likely enhanced quality: Modifiability. Likely trade-off: Performance (latency).
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q01122 — Publish-Subscribe (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Publish-Subscribe to address this requirement: The Student Portal must notify an unknown and changing set of interested users/components whenever a seat becomes available in a preferred class, without the event producer knowing every recipient.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the component that detects or produces the scenario event is the Publisher; interested users, channels, or components are Subscribers; the event distributor/channel is the publish-subscribe connector. The Publisher announces the event without naming every recipient, and the distributor delivers it to the currently registered interested Subscribers.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q01218 — Publish-Subscribe (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Online Learning Platform  

In the Online Learning Platform, Publish-Subscribe is used as described: The Learning Platform must notify an unknown and changing set of interested users/components whenever a new lesson is released, without the event producer knowing every recipient.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Modifiability** because decouples producers from consumers so subscribers can be added/removed without changing publisher correctness.
Threatened: **Performance (latency)** because event distribution adds latency; ordering and delivery may be less controlled or guaranteed and broadcast can waste work.

## Q01281 — Shared-Data (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Shared-Data** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: allow multiple independent computational components to persistently share and manipulate data that belongs to no single component.
- Mechanism: mediates producers and consumers through persistent shared storage so they need not directly know each other.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Shared-data store, Data accessor) and relation/connector (data reading/writing connector) to the concrete Student Portal.
- Likely enhanced quality: Modifiability. Likely trade-off: Performance.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01282 — Shared-Data (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Shared-Data to address this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the authoritative repository holding the scenario's shared records is the Shared-Data Store; the independent application components that read or write those records are Data Accessors. Accessors communicate indirectly by reading/writing the repository rather than calling one another to exchange the shared state, so consistency and ownership rules must be defined at the store boundary.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01283 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality trade-off  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

In the University Student Portal, Shared-Data is used as described: Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Modifiability** because mediates producers and consumers through persistent shared storage so they need not directly know each other.
Threatened: **Performance** because the store can bottleneck or fail centrally, while accessors remain coupled to shared schema and consistency/security concerns.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01285 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

A team designing the University Student Portal is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Student Portal need to persistently read and write the same timetable and academic records; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Shared-Data** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: allow multiple independent computational components to persistently share and manipulate data that belongs to no single component. Shared-Data centers on Shared-data store, Data accessor and data reading/writing connector; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Music Streaming Service  

For the Music Streaming Service, assume the architect has chosen Shared-Data to address this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Music Streaming Platform need to persistently read and write the same playlists and listening history; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the authoritative repository holding the scenario's shared records is the Shared-Data Store; the independent application components that read or write those records are Data Accessors. Accessors communicate indirectly by reading/writing the repository rather than calling one another to exchange the shared state, so consistency and ownership rules must be defined at the store boundary.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01343 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Scenario:** Music Streaming Service  

In the Music Streaming Service, Shared-Data is used as described: Multiple independent components of the Music Streaming Platform need to persistently read and write the same playlists and listening history; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

## Q01345 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Music Streaming Service  

A team designing the Music Streaming Service is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Music Streaming Platform need to persistently read and write the same playlists and listening history; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Shared-Data** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: allow multiple independent computational components to persistently share and manipulate data that belongs to no single component. Shared-Data centers on Shared-data store, Data accessor and data reading/writing connector; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Shared-Data** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: allow multiple independent computational components to persistently share and manipulate data that belongs to no single component. Shared-Data centers on Shared-data store, Data accessor and data reading/writing connector; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q01372 — Shared-Data (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Hotel Booking Platform  

For the Hotel Booking Platform, assume the architect has chosen Shared-Data to address this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Hotel Booking Platform need to persistently read and write the same reservations and room inventory; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the authoritative repository holding the scenario's shared records is the Shared-Data Store; the independent application components that read or write those records are Data Accessors. Accessors communicate indirectly by reading/writing the repository rather than calling one another to exchange the shared state, so consistency and ownership rules must be defined at the store boundary.

</details>

**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Telecommunications Billing  

In the Telecommunications Billing, Shared-Data is used as described: Multiple independent components of the Telecom Billing Platform need to persistently read and write the same usage and invoices; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and a different quality attribute that may be threatened. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Modifiability** because mediates producers and consumers through persistent shared storage so they need not directly know each other.
Threatened: **Performance** because the store can bottleneck or fail centrally, while accessors remain coupled to shared schema and consistency/security concerns.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01399 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Telecommunications Billing  

An architect claims that once Shared-Data is selected for the Telecommunications Billing, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Telecom Billing Platform need to persistently read and write the same usage and invoices; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **data accessors interact through shared data store(s)** and the weakness **the store can bottleneck or fail centrally, while accessors remain coupled to shared schema and consistency/security concerns**. Construct an edge case where the intended mechanism is missing, overloaded or becomes a single dependency and show why the desired end-to-end quality is not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01400 — Shared-Data vs Client-Server (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Telecommunications Billing  

A team designing the Telecommunications Billing is split between **Shared-Data** and **Client-Server** for the following requirement:
Multiple independent components of the Telecom Billing Platform need to persistently read and write the same usage and invoices; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Shared-Data** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: allow multiple independent computational components to persistently share and manipulate data that belongs to no single component. Shared-Data centers on Shared-data store, Data accessor and data reading/writing connector; **Client-Server** instead addresses: provide shared services/resources to distributed clients through asymmetric request/reply interactions. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: users on distributed devices retrieve centrally managed online services/data.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_7_CCPatterns_Client-Server.pdf

</details>

## Q01401 — Shared-Data (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

Digital Library: Multiple independent components of the Digital Library need to persistently read and write the same catalog and borrowing history; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Shared-Data** (C&C Pattern).
- Architectural problem: allow multiple independent computational components to persistently share and manipulate data that belongs to no single component.
- Mechanism: mediates producers and consumers through persistent shared storage so they need not directly know each other.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Shared-data store, Data accessor) and relation/connector (data reading/writing connector) to the concrete Digital Library.
- Likely enhanced quality: Modifiability. Likely trade-off: Performance.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01402 — Shared-Data (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

For the Digital Library, assume the architect has chosen Shared-Data to address this requirement: Multiple independent components of the Digital Library need to persistently read and write the same catalog and borrowing history; the information does not belong exclusively to any one component.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the authoritative repository holding the scenario's shared records is the Shared-Data Store; the independent application components that read or write those records are Data Accessors. Accessors communicate indirectly by reading/writing the repository rather than calling one another to exchange the shared state, so consistency and ownership rules must be defined at the store boundary.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q01441 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must analyze multi-year learning analytics logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Map-Reduce** (Allocation Pattern).
- Architectural problem: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation.
- Mechanism: runs many map instances across processors, shuffles/sorts key-value output, then combines results in reduce functions while infrastructure deploys, monitors and recovers tasks.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Map, Reduce, Infrastructure) and relation/connector (infrastructure-managed key/value data movement) to the concrete Student Portal.
- Likely enhanced quality: Performance. Mechanism: parallel Map and Reduce instances can increase batch throughput. Likely weakness: Performance can degrade when framework overhead or partition skew outweighs parallelism.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01442 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Map-Reduce to address this requirement: The Student Portal must analyze multi-year learning analytics logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the large input/log files are partitioned by the Infrastructure; Map workers transform each partition into intermediate key/value records; shuffle/sort groups equal keys; Reduce workers aggregate each group into the required result. The Infrastructure distributes tasks, moves intermediate data, monitors workers, and reruns failed work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01443 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

In the University Student Portal, Map-Reduce is used as described: The Student Portal must analyze multi-year learning analytics logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded condition under which that benefit can be lost. Explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.

## Q01455 — Map-Reduce vs Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

A team designing the Electricity Utility App is split between **Map-Reduce** and **Pipe-and-Filter** for the following requirement:
The Utility Application must analyze national smart-meter history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Map-Reduce** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation. Map-Reduce centers on Map, Reduce, Infrastructure and infrastructure-managed key/value data movement; **Pipe-and-Filter** instead addresses: perform successive transformations of a stream using independent reusable processing stages. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: input data undergoes a sequence of transformations before becoming output.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Map-Reduce** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation. <details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Map-Reduce** (Allocation Pattern).
- Architectural problem: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation.

- Map the source-grounded elements (Map, Reduce, Infrastructure) and relation/connector (infrastructure-managed key/value data movement) to the concrete Hospital Information System.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

## Q01483 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Hospital Information System  

In the Hospital Information System, Map-Reduce is used as described: The Hospital Information System must analyze de-identified clinical records at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded condition under which that benefit can be lost. Explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.

</details>

## Q01507 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Cloud File Storage  

For the Cloud File Storage, assume the architect has chosen Map-Reduce to address this requirement: The Cloud Storage Platform must analyze storage-access audit logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the large input/log files are partitioned by the Infrastructure; Map workers transform each partition into intermediate key/value records; shuffle/sort groups equal keys; Reduce workers aggregate each group into the required result. The Infrastructure distributes tasks, moves intermediate data, monitors workers, and reruns failed work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01508 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Cloud File Storage  

In the Cloud File Storage, Map-Reduce is used as described: The Cloud Storage Platform must analyze storage-access audit logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded condition under which that benefit can be lost. Explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded condition under which that benefit can be lost. Explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.

**Type:** Compare and distinguish

A team designing the Hotel Booking Platform is split between **Map-Reduce** and **Pipe-and-Filter** for the following requirement:
The Hotel Booking Platform must analyze search and occupancy history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Map-Reduce** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation. Map-Reduce centers on Map, Reduce, Infrastructure and infrastructure-managed key/value data movement; **Pipe-and-Filter** instead addresses: perform successive transformations of a stream using independent reusable processing stages. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: input data undergoes a sequence of transformations before becoming output.

Prefer **Map-Reduce** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation. ## Q01562 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

For the Digital Library, assume the architect has chosen Map-Reduce to address this requirement: The Digital Library must analyze catalog/search logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the large input/log files are partitioned by the Infrastructure; Map workers transform each partition into intermediate key/value records; shuffle/sort groups equal keys; Reduce workers aggregate each group into the required result. The Infrastructure distributes tasks, moves intermediate data, monitors workers, and reruns failed work.

## Q01563 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

In the Digital Library, Map-Reduce is used as described: The Digital Library must analyze catalog/search logs at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded condition under which that benefit can be lost. Explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q01564 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 5 marks)

## Q01587 — Map-Reduce (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Event Ticketing Platform  

For the Event Ticketing Platform, assume the architect has chosen Map-Reduce to address this requirement: The Ticketing Platform must analyze ticket search and sales history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: the large input/log files are partitioned by the Infrastructure; Map workers transform each partition into intermediate key/value records; shuffle/sort groups equal keys; Reduce workers aggregate each group into the required result. The Infrastructure distributes tasks, moves intermediate data, monitors workers, and reruns failed work.

</details>

## Q01588 — Map-Reduce (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Event Ticketing Platform  

In the Event Ticketing Platform, Map-Reduce is used as described: The Ticketing Platform must analyze ticket search and sales history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded condition under which that benefit can be lost. Explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Performance** because many Map instances process partitions concurrently and Reduce instances combine grouped results, increasing batch throughput.
Weakness: **Performance** can degrade when framework startup, shuffle/sort and synchronization overhead dominate a small workload, or when partition skew leaves one worker as the straggler.

</details>

**Type:** Compare and distinguish
