The Ticketing Platform must analyze ticket search and sales history at very large scale by dividing work across many processors, with infrastructure responsible for distributing tasks and recovering failed workers.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Map-Reduce** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: process very large file-based data sets efficiently and resiliently using massively parallel computation. Map-Reduce centers on Map, Reduce, Infrastructure and infrastructure-managed key/value data movement; **Pipe-and-Filter** instead addresses: perform successive transformations of a stream using independent reusable processing stages. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: input data undergoes a sequence of transformations before becoming output.

## Q01601 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 6 marks)

**Type:** Scenario application  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

University Student Portal: The Student Portal must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Multi-Tier** (Allocation Pattern).
- Architectural problem: separate runtime components into logical tiers with constrained communication and potentially map them onto different computing platforms.
- Mechanism: groups computationally independent runtime components and constrains cross-tier communication, permitting specialized deployment, scaling and security policies.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Tier (logical grouping of runtime components)) and relation/connector (communicates-with relation, allocated-to relation) to the concrete Student Portal.
- Likely enhanced quality: Security. Likely weakness: substantial hardware, software, design and operational cost/complexity.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01602 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

For the University Student Portal, assume the architect has chosen Multi-Tier to address this requirement: The Student Portal must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: user-interface runtime components form the presentation tier, application/business processing forms the application tier, and persistent records/services form the data tier. Request/reply communication crosses the permitted tier boundaries, and each tier is allocated to its own deployable runtime/platform so it can be secured or scaled independently; each component belongs to one tier.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

For the Cloud File Storage, assume the architect has chosen Multi-Tier to address this requirement: The Cloud Storage Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

## Q01670 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Cloud File Storage  

A team designing the Cloud File Storage is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Cloud Storage Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Multi-Tier** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: separate runtime components into logical tiers with constrained communication and potentially map them onto different computing platforms. Multi-Tier centers on Tier (logical grouping of runtime components) and communicates-with relation; **Layer** instead addresses: separate implementation responsibilities so concerns can evolve relatively independently. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: UI/business/data concerns must be separated so changes can be localized.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **a software component belongs to exactly one tier** and the weakness **adds hardware/software/design/operational cost and complexity that may not be justified for small systems**. </details>

## Q01695 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Hotel Booking Platform  

A team designing the Hotel Booking Platform is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Hotel Booking Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Multi-Tier** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: separate runtime components into logical tiers with constrained communication and potentially map them onto different computing platforms. Multi-Tier centers on Tier (logical grouping of runtime components) and communicates-with relation; **Layer** instead addresses: separate implementation responsibilities so concerns can evolve relatively independently. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: UI/business/data concerns must be separated so changes can be localized.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

Digital Library: The Digital Library must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Select the most suitable architectural pattern and justify it in scenario-specific terms. Your justification must identify the architectural problem, the relevant elements/relations, and one quality attribute consequence.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Best fit: **Multi-Tier** (Allocation Pattern).
- Architectural problem: separate runtime components into logical tiers with constrained communication and potentially map them onto different computing platforms.
- Mechanism: groups computationally independent runtime components and constrains cross-tier communication, permitting specialized deployment, scaling and security policies.
- Map the source-grounded elements (Tier (logical grouping of runtime components)) and relation/connector (communicates-with relation, allocated-to relation) to the concrete Digital Library.
- Likely enhanced quality: Security. Likely weakness: substantial hardware, software, design and operational cost/complexity.
Full credit requires scenario-specific reasoning, not only the pattern name.

**Exam trap:** Naming a familiar pattern without explaining why its mechanism solves this exact requirement.

**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01722 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

For the Digital Library, assume the architect has chosen Multi-Tier to address this requirement: The Digital Library must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: user-interface runtime components form the presentation tier, application/business processing forms the application tier, and persistent records/services form the data tier. Request/reply communication crosses the permitted tier boundaries, and each tier is allocated to its own deployable runtime/platform so it can be secured or scaled independently; each component belongs to one tier.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01723 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Quality benefit and weakness  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q1/Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

In the Digital Library, Multi-Tier is used as described: The Digital Library must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded weakness of the pattern. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Security** because groups computationally independent runtime components and constrains cross-tier communication, permitting specialized deployment, scaling and security policies.
Weakness: substantial **cost and complexity** because separate tiers add hardware, software, design, implementation and operational overhead that may not be justified for a simple system.
Qualify the claim ('may/can') and tie each effect to an element, connector, constraint or deployment decision.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01724 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

An architect claims that once Multi-Tier is selected for the Digital Library, its expected quality benefits are guaranteed. Critique the claim using this requirement: The Digital Library must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Use at least one source-grounded constraint or weakness and give a concrete failure/edge case.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Reject the guarantee. Patterns are reusable design decisions, not quality guarantees. Use a constraint such as **a software component belongs to exactly one tier** and the weakness **adds hardware/software/design/operational cost and complexity that may not be justified for small systems**. Construct an edge case where the intended mechanism is missing, overloaded or becomes a single dependency and show why the desired end-to-end quality is not achieved.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q01725 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Library  

A team designing the Digital Library is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Digital Library must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Multi-Tier** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: separate runtime components into logical tiers with constrained communication and potentially map them onto different computing platforms. Multi-Tier centers on Tier (logical grouping of runtime components) and communicates-with relation; **Layer** instead addresses: separate implementation responsibilities so concerns can evolve relatively independently. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: UI/business/data concerns must be separated so changes can be localized.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

In the Event Ticketing Platform, Multi-Tier is used as described: The Ticketing Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Explain one quality attribute that the pattern may enhance and one source-grounded weakness of the pattern. For each, explain the mechanism rather than merely naming the quality or weakness.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Enhanced: **Security** because groups computationally independent runtime components and constrains cross-tier communication, permitting specialized deployment, scaling and security policies.
Weakness: substantial **cost and complexity** because separate tiers add hardware, software, design, implementation and operational overhead that may not be justified for a simple system.

</details>

## Q01749 — Multi-Tier (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Constraint / failure reasoning

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

## Q01750 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Compare and distinguish  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Event Ticketing Platform  

A team designing the Event Ticketing Platform is split between **Multi-Tier** and **Layer** for the following requirement:
The Ticketing Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Compare the two at the architectural level. Decide which better matches the requirement, explain the decisive distinction, and identify one circumstance that could make the alternative preferable.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Prefer **Multi-Tier** for the stated requirement because its core problem is: separate runtime components into logical tiers with constrained communication and potentially map them onto different computing platforms. Multi-Tier centers on Tier (logical grouping of runtime components) and communicates-with relation; **Layer** instead addresses: separate implementation responsibilities so concerns can evolve relatively independently. The alternative becomes preferable if the requirement shifts toward: UI/business/data concerns must be separated so changes can be localized.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q01752 — Multi-Tier (Hard, 4 marks)

**Type:** Elements and relations  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Online Auction Platform  

For the Online Auction Platform, assume the architect has chosen Multi-Tier to address this requirement: The Auction Platform must separate runtime presentation, application processing, and data services into computational groups that can be deployed, secured and scaled on different platforms with constrained cross-group communication.

Describe the pattern elements and connectors/relations in this concrete scenario. Do not give only generic definitions.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Concrete mapping for **University Student Portal**: user-interface runtime components form the presentation tier, application/business processing forms the application tier, and persistent records/services form the data tier. Request/reply communication crosses the permitted tier boundaries, and each tier is allocated to its own deployable runtime/platform so it can be secured or scaled independently; each component belongs to one tier.

</details>

## Q03673 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

In the University Student Portal, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03674 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal must distribute events related to 'a seat becomes available in a preferred class'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

List-based keeps subscription lists and is runtime-efficient but less decoupled. Broadcast-based reduces publisher knowledge but can waste work because subscribers inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matches event attributes against subscriber-defined patterns and is the most expressive for selective predicates, at the cost of matching/distribution complexity. Tie the choice to modifiability versus runtime overhead.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03675 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

In a P2P feature for the University Student Portal, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03676 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the University Student Portal by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03677 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q03678 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03679 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03680 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal uses Map-Reduce on multi-year learning analytics logs. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03681 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

A diagram for the University Student Portal labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03691 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

In the Electricity Utility App, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03692 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

The Electricity Utility App must distribute events related to 'consumption exceeds a threshold'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

List-based keeps subscription lists and is runtime-efficient but less decoupled. Broadcast-based reduces publisher knowledge but can waste work because subscribers inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matches event attributes against subscriber-defined patterns and is the most expressive for selective predicates, at the cost of matching/distribution complexity. Tie the choice to modifiability versus runtime overhead.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03693 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

In a P2P feature for the Electricity Utility App, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03694 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the Electricity Utility App by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03695 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

The Electricity Utility App uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

## Q03696 — Shared-Data (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

The Electricity Utility App uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03697 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

The Electricity Utility App displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03698 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Electricity Utility App  

The Electricity Utility App uses Map-Reduce on national smart-meter history. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03724 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

The E-Commerce Marketplace displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03725 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

The E-Commerce Marketplace uses Map-Reduce on clickstream and order history. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03726 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** E-Commerce Marketplace  

A diagram for the E-Commerce Marketplace labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03727 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Banking App  

In the Digital Banking App, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03728 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Banking App  

The Digital Banking App must distribute events related to 'a suspicious transaction is detected'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

List-based keeps subscription lists and is runtime-efficient but less decoupled. Broadcast-based reduces publisher knowledge but can waste work because subscribers inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matches event attributes against subscriber-defined patterns and is the most expressive for selective predicates, at the cost of matching/distribution complexity. Tie the choice to modifiability versus runtime overhead.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03729 — Peer-to-Peer (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Discovery, hops and supernodes  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Digital Banking App  

In a P2P feature for the Digital Banking App, peers cannot broadcast discovery indefinitely. Explain the role of search propagation, **hop limits**, and **supernodes**, and show one quality trade-off caused by tightening the hop limit.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Search may propagate peer-to-peer for a bounded number of hops; hop limits control network overhead. Specialized peers/supernodes may index or route searches so ordinary peers reach more resources efficiently. A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03730 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Banking App  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the Digital Banking App by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03731 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Digital Banking App  

The Digital Banking App uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

A tighter hop limit can improve performance/network overhead/predictability but reduce discoverability/availability of rare resources. A supernode can improve discovery but may concentrate responsibility and require availability/security hardening.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_8_CCPatterns_Peer-to-Peer.pdf

</details>

## Q03757 — Pipe-and-Filter (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Pipeline parallelism  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

Three items T1, T2 and T3 are processed in the Smart Traffic Platform by Filter A→Filter B→Filter C. Give a valid simultaneous execution snapshot, explain how buffering enables it, then identify why this improves **throughput** without necessarily reducing the end-to-end **latency** of one item.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Example snapshot: A processes T3, B processes T2, C processes T1. Pipes/buffers decouple stage timing until buffers fill, allowing concurrent stage execution. This can increase aggregate throughput because several items are in flight, but T1 still must traverse all mandatory stages, so its own end-to-end latency may remain the sum of stage/queue delays.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_6_CCPatterns_Pipe and Filter.pdf

</details>

## Q03758 — Service-Oriented Architecture (Brutal, 7 marks)

**Type:** ESB, registry, orchestration  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q3  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

The Smart Traffic Platform uses SOA. Distinguish the roles of a **service registry**, **ESB**, and **orchestration server**. For each, give one benefit and one new risk/overhead. Explain why none of the three is automatically required in every SOA instance.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Registry: providers register and consumers discover services, hiding provider location/identity and improving modifiability; adds discovery dependency/complexity. ESB: routes/transforms protocols/content and can perform security checks, improving interoperability/modifiability; adds latency and failure point. Orchestration server: coordinates multi-service business workflows; adds centralized coordination complexity/failure risk. They are optional architectural elements chosen according to the specific SOA problem.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_9_CCPatterns_Service-Oriented-Architecture.pdf

</details>

**Type:** Replication and coupling  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

The Smart Traffic Platform uses Shared-Data. The architect replicates the data store across two regions to reduce outage risk. Explain what quality may improve, then identify two new issues introduced by replication and one coupling problem that remains even if producers/consumers do not know each other.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Replication can improve availability and possibly read performance. New issues include consistency/synchronization, conflict resolution, replication latency, failover routing and operational complexity. Producer/consumer identity coupling is reduced, but accessors can still be coupled through knowledge of the shared **data schema/structure**.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_11_CCPatterns_Shared-Data.pdf

</details>

## Q03760 — Model-View-Controller (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Many views and constraints  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

The Smart Traffic Platform displays the same model through a table, chart and mobile visualization. Explain how MVC keeps them synchronized, why many views/controllers can share one model, and why the lecture constraint that the model should not directly interact with the controller matters.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Model holds application data/state and notifies views of changes; views render/query model; controllers translate user gestures into model/view actions. Multiple views/controllers can share one model because presentation/input concerns are separated. Preventing direct model→controller dependency helps preserve separation and reduces coupling; notifications from model go to interested views rather than making model dependent on specific input-control logic.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_5_CCPatterns_Model-view Controller.pdf

</details>

## Q03761 — Map-Reduce (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Partition imbalance  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

The Smart Traffic Platform uses Map-Reduce on city-wide traffic sensor archive. One partition contains 70% of the data while the others are tiny. Explain why adding more processors may fail to improve completion time and connect the answer to the pattern's constraints and overhead.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Map-Reduce benefits depend on dividing the data into similar-sized subsets. A dominant partition becomes a straggler/bottleneck, leaving other processors idle and eroding parallel speedup. Infrastructure still incurs deployment/shuffle/sort/monitoring overhead. Stateless maps/key-value communication do not solve skew automatically; data partitioning must support balanced work.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_12_AllocationPatterns_Map-Reduce.pdf

</details>

## Q03762 — Multi-Tier vs Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Distinction  
**Exam family:** Past Paper Q4  
**Scenario:** Smart Traffic Platform  

A diagram for the Smart Traffic Platform labels 'Presentation', 'Business' and 'Data'. A student concludes it is definitely a Layer pattern. Explain why the labels alone are insufficient and show how the **same names** could describe either Layer or Multi-Tier depending on element/relation semantics.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Layer is a **module pattern**: implementation units grouped into layers with allowed-to-use dependency rules. Multi-Tier is an **allocation/runtime pattern**: runtime components grouped into tiers with communication/allocation constraints. Box labels do not determine semantics. Ask whether the elements are modules and dependencies, or runtime components/tier groupings mapped to platforms.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf; Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_13_AllocationPatterns_Multi-Tier.pdf

</details>

## Q03763 — Layer (Brutal, 5 marks)

**Type:** Bridging and upward calls  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Ride-Hailing Platform  

In the Ride-Hailing Platform, a strict Layer design is A→B→C. The team proposes (i) A directly uses C for performance and (ii) C emits a one-way callback/event upward to A without depending on a returned answer. Analyze both proposals using the lecture's finer points.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

A→C is **bridging**: it may be permitted, but must be explicitly documented; it can reduce traversal overhead while weakening dependency restriction/modifiability. An **upward call** is not automatically an upward *use*: the lecture defines 'uses' in terms of depending on the answer. A one-way upward notification can be allowed if it does not create a dependency on a response. Be explicit about the relation semantics.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_2_ModulePatterns_Layer Pattern.pdf

</details>

## Q03764 — Publish-Subscribe (Brutal, 6 marks)

**Type:** Variant selection  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** Ride-Hailing Platform  

The Ride-Hailing Platform must distribute events related to 'a driver accepts the trip'. Compare **list-based, broadcast-based and content-based** Publish-Subscribe. Choose a variant for a case with many subscribers but highly selective event predicates and justify the trade-off.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

List-based keeps subscription lists and is runtime-efficient but less decoupled. Broadcast-based reduces publisher knowledge but can waste work because subscribers inspect irrelevant events. Content-based matches event attributes against subscriber-defined patterns and is the most expressive for selective predicates, at the cost of matching/distribution complexity. Tie the choice to modifiability versus runtime overhead.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_10_CCPatterns_Publish-Subscribe.pdf

</details>

## Q03781 — Other Allocation Patterns (Very Hard, 5 marks)

**Type:** Work assignment patterns  
**Exam family:** Extended  
**Scenario:** University Student Portal  

The University Student Portal will be developed by teams across three countries. Compare the **Platform**, **Competence Center**, and **Open Source** work-assignment patterns and choose one for a situation where one site has unique security expertise.

<details><summary>Answer framework / marking outline</summary>

Platform: one site develops reusable core assets while other sites build applications using them. Competence Center: allocate work according to technical/domain expertise - best fit when one site has unique security expertise. Open Source: many independent contributors with minimal centralized control except integration strategy. Discuss coordination/control versus expertise/autonomy trade-offs.



**Grounding:** Lecture4_ArchitecturalPatterns_14_AllocationPatterns_Other Allocation Patterns.pdf

</details>

Open Source: many independent contributors with minimal centralized control except integration strategy. Discuss coordination/control versus expertise/autonomy trade-offs.

</details>
